rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation changes initial max_val from -INFINITY to -1e10f. For input [16,64,128] with typical pool params, total_elements=32768<65536, so mutated kernel is used. When all window values < -1e10 (e.g., -1e15), original outputs correct max (-1e15), mutant outputs -1e10. Difference ~1e15 >> tolerance 1e13.
rounds.survival_reason: Layer 2 testing only used random values in approximately [-4, 4] range and stress tests with minimum around -4. These values are all greater than -1e10, so the mutated initial value -1e10f was always overwritten by actual input values. The mutation only manifests when pooling windows contain exclusively values below -1e10, which was never tested.
rounds.kill_strategy: Create input tensor filled entirely with values less than -1e10 (e.g., -1e15). Every pooling window will have all values below the mutated initial -1e10f, causing mutant to output -1e10 instead of the correct maximum.
rounds.recommendations: Stress testing for reduction operations should include extreme negative values approaching -INFINITY to verify correct initialization of accumulators. Values like -1e20, -1e30, or -FLT_MAX should be tested to catch finite-initial-value mutations.
rounds.suggested_code:
def generate_inputs(device):
    # All values are -1e15, far below the mutant's -1e10 initial max_val
    # Original with -INFINITY will correctly find max = -1e15
    # Mutant with -1e10 will never update (since -1e15 < -1e10), outputting -1e10
    x = torch.full((16, 64, 128), -1e15, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    return [x]
